_doc: Per-tool response-size regression test fixtures (v1.1.1 P1 of the Atlas Phase 6 strategy).
_purpose: Each fixture runs one tool with the given args, measures the response body in bytes, and fails CI if it exceeds cap_bytes. Catches drift where a tool quietly grows its response size between releases.
_strategy_origin: atlas-phase6-strategy-adjusted-2026-04-30: thin <= 400B, standard <= 1.5KB, full uncapped. Those targets are PER RESULT for the strategy's aspirational thin-mode work. This fixture file uses TODAY'S response sizes (with small headroom) as the regression bar, so any drift fails CI. Going FORWARD, when v1.1.2 adds explicit thin-mode flags to tools, add separate fixtures here for the thin variant with the strategy's per-result caps.
_when_to_update_caps: If a feature adds fields a tool legitimately needs to return, bump the cap with a justification comment in this file. Don't loosen a cap without one. If a tool's response shape gets TIGHTER (e.g., a new thin mode), prefer adding a NEW fixture for that mode rather than editing an existing cap.
_run: npm run test:byte-caps   # standalone   |   npm run test:arch   # chained
_runtime_requirement: A live Lore daemon at http://127.0.0.1:3847 with auth.token. If unreachable, the test exits 0 with a warning so it's safe in CI environments without a daemon.

fixtures.rationale: Fixed-size graph statistics; node count, edge count, type breakdown for one workspace. Sprint L2: workspace is required, no silent fallback.
One-shot daemon health check. Fixed shape.

Full-text search with limit=5. Each LoreNode currently includes full content+tags+metadata; 5 hits average ~1.6KB each. Cap reflects today's shape with ~50% headroom. v1.1.2 follow-up: add a thin mode that returns id+label+type+project only (~200B/hit); a separate fixture here will measure that path.

Search with no keyword matches. Exercises the negative-evidence path of P2: confidence 0 + reason string only. (Note: graph keyword search is the path used here, not verbatim semantic — keyword has true zero-result outcomes whereas semantic always returns something.)

Summary mode caps response at ~2KB per the in-tool comment, but real responses run 1.5–4KB depending on hit count. 10 hits at ~448B each = ~4.5KB plus envelope. Cap raised 6000 → 9000 by Sprint L7 (2026-05-24): pre-Sprint-L the harness omitted workspace and the validation error fit under 6KB, so the real shape was never measured. First real measurement on the default workspace was 7378B; 9000B preserves ~20% headroom against today's knowledge graph (now larger than the dev-workspace baseline the 6KB cap was sized for).

Recall on a low-relevance topic — semantic search ALWAYS returns something (top-K by similarity), so the response shape is the same as a normal recall. v1.1.2 follow-up: when verbatim similarity scores are plumbed through (parked in V1.1_DEFERRED), this fixture can become a true negative-evidence test that drops to ~1KB on low-score results.

Re-enabled by Sprint 7 (2026-05-24). list_nodes now cursor-paginates with default limit=100; first-page response on the default workspace's 144 decision nodes fits well under the 64 KB cap (each entry carries id+type+label+tags+project+updatedAt only, ~170-450B/node). Callers wanting more nodes pass `cursor` from the prior response. Pre-Sprint-7 the tool returned every match in one shot (observed 2.4 MB = 38× the cap); the fixture sat in _deferred_fixtures with that observation noted.

QA finding B3 (round E, 2026-09-03) — added with the pagination fix; had NO fixture at all before this (confirmed via grep), so a 2000-collection workspace's ~1.2MiB unbounded response would have silently passed CI. Default call now cursor-paginates at DEFAULT_SCHEMA_LIST_LIMIT=100 entries with rowCount omitted (withCounts defaults false) — same shape/cap story as list_nodes above, which this mirrors: each entry is name+columns+primaryKey only, well under 64KB for 100 entries regardless of how many collections the workspace actually has declared. Callers wanting more pass the response's nextCursor. If this workspace has fewer than 100 collections declared, the measured size will be much smaller than the cap; the cap exists to catch the default page ever growing unbounded again, not to pin today's exact size.

QA finding B3 (round E, 2026-09-03) — added alongside collection_schema_list; also had no fixture. Deliberately probes a collection name that (almost certainly) doesn't exist so the response is the fixed-shape `null` regardless of what any given developer's default workspace has declared (mirrors the 'no keyword matches' negative-evidence pattern used for the `search` fixture above) — a real hit would return the full CollectionSchema (name+fields[]), which is workspace-dependent and not a stable regression target the way the not-found shape is.

_deferred_fixtures_note: Fixtures moved out of the active set during Sprint L7 (2026-05-24) because their first real measurement (after the harness started passing workspace) was >2× the previously-aspirational cap. Per L7 spec scope guard, these need operator decision — either re-shape the tool's response, narrow the fixture args, or accept a substantially higher cap — before they return to the active set. Do NOT silently re-enable. The 2026-06-13 entries are different: they probe Atlas-domain code tools that Lore Core no longer serves (Atlas externalized as a client in v3.11.0), so a Core-only daemon returns 'Tool not found' and the suite fails on every host that has a live daemon. They belong in an Atlas-side byte-caps suite, not Core's.

_deferred_fixtures._deferred_reason: 2026-06-13: Atlas-domain tool, not served by Lore Core (Atlas externalized in v3.11.0). Returned MCP -32602 'Tool code_blast_radius not found' against the live Core daemon, failing test:arch on any host with a daemon up. Re-home in an Atlas byte-caps suite.
_deferred_fixtures.rationale: v1.1.1 P2 — exercises the negative-evidence path on an unknown symbol. Response is { error, _meta:{confidence:0, negative_evidence, sources_consulted} }. Should be tight; if it grows past 800B the negative-evidence message has bloated and needs trimming.

_deferred_fixtures._deferred_reason: 2026-06-13: Atlas-domain tool, not served by Lore Core (Atlas externalized in v3.11.0). Returned MCP -32602 'Tool code_cycles not found' against the live Core daemon, failing test:arch on any host with a daemon up. Re-home in an Atlas byte-caps suite.
_deferred_fixtures.rationale: Cycle detection over the parsed graph. Response carries the cycles list + the v1.1.1 P2 _meta envelope. Bumped from 4000 → 8000 on 2026-05-10: codebase growth has produced more legitimately-detected cycles (observed ~6700B). Future tightening lever: add a thin mode that returns just the cycle ids (no member-symbol detail) and put a separate fixture on the thin variant rather than re-shrinking this cap.
